q22594.en: In one second you travel about 14 m if you are driving at 50 km/h.

explain.short: 50 km/h divided by 3.6 is about 14 metres every second. So in one second of reaction you travel about 14 m.
explain.rule: Divide km/h by 3.6: 50 = 14 m, 100 = 28 m, 130 = 36 m, 150 = 42 m in one second.
explain.trap: Check the pair 'm 14' and '50 km/h': here they match (km/h divided by 3.6).

sceneParams.caption: 50 km/h = about 14 m every second

q22595.en: In one second you travel about 28 m if you are driving at 100 km/h.

explain.short: 100 km/h divided by 3.6 is about 28 metres every second. So in one second of reaction you travel about 28 m.
explain.rule: Divide km/h by 3.6: 50 = 14 m, 100 = 28 m, 130 = 36 m, 150 = 42 m in one second.
explain.trap: Check the pair 'm 28' and '100 km/h': here they match (km/h divided by 3.6).

sceneParams.caption: 100 km/h = about 28 m every second

q22596.en: In one second you travel about 36 m if you are driving at 130 km/h.

explain.short: 130 km/h divided by 3.6 is about 36 metres every second. So in one second of reaction you travel about 36 m.
explain.rule: Divide km/h by 3.6: 50 = 14 m, 100 = 28 m, 130 = 36 m, 150 = 42 m in one second.
explain.trap: Check the pair 'm 36' and '130 km/h': here they match (km/h divided by 3.6).

sceneParams.caption: 130 km/h = about 36 m every second

q22597.en: In one second you travel about 42 m if you are driving at 150 km/h.

explain.short: 150 km/h divided by 3.6 is about 42 metres every second. So in one second of reaction you travel about 42 m.
explain.rule: Divide km/h by 3.6: 50 = 14 m, 100 = 28 m, 130 = 36 m, 150 = 42 m in one second.
explain.trap: Check the pair 'm 42' and '150 km/h': here they match (km/h divided by 3.6).

sceneParams.caption: 150 km/h = about 42 m every second

q22598.en: In one second you travel about 20 m if you are driving at 150 km/h.

explain.short: 150 km/h divided by 3.6 is about 42 metres every second, not 20 m. The number in the statement is wrong.
explain.rule: Divide km/h by 3.6: 50 = 14 m, 100 = 28 m, 130 = 36 m, 150 = 42 m in one second.
explain.trap: 'm 20' is the wrong number for 150 km/h: the right value is about 42 m.

sceneParams.caption: 150 km/h = about 42 m per second, not 20 m

q22599.en: In one second you travel about 4 m if you are driving at 50 km/h.

explain.short: 50 km/h divided by 3.6 is about 14 metres every second, not 4 m. The number in the statement is wrong.
explain.rule: Divide km/h by 3.6: 50 = 14 m, 100 = 28 m, 130 = 36 m, 150 = 42 m in one second.
explain.trap: 'm 4' is the wrong number for 50 km/h: the right value is about 14 m.

sceneParams.caption: 50 km/h = about 14 m per second, not 4 m

q22600.en: In one second you travel about 10 m if you are driving at 100 km/h.

explain.short: 100 km/h divided by 3.6 is about 28 metres every second, not 10 m. The number in the statement is wrong.
explain.rule: Divide km/h by 3.6: 50 = 14 m, 100 = 28 m, 130 = 36 m, 150 = 42 m in one second.
explain.trap: 'm 10' is the wrong number for 100 km/h: the right value is about 28 m.

sceneParams.caption: 100 km/h = about 28 m per second, not 10 m

q22601.en: In one second you travel about 15 m if you are driving at 130 km/h.

explain.short: 130 km/h divided by 3.6 is about 36 metres every second, not 15 m. The number in the statement is wrong.
explain.rule: Divide km/h by 3.6: 50 = 14 m, 100 = 28 m, 130 = 36 m, 150 = 42 m in one second.
explain.trap: 'm 15' is the wrong number for 130 km/h: the right value is about 36 m.

sceneParams.caption: 130 km/h = about 36 m per second, not 15 m

q22602.en: The braking distance is the distance travelled from the start of braking until the vehicle stops.

explain.short: This is the definition of braking distance: it starts when the brakes begin to work and ends when the car is still.
explain.rule: Braking distance grows with the square of speed: 2x speed = 4x, 3x = 9x, 4x = 16x.
explain.trap: Do not confuse it with the reaction distance, which comes BEFORE 'l'inizio della frenata' (the start of braking).

sceneParams.caption: Braking distance: from brake to full stop

q22603.en: The braking distance becomes four times longer if the speed doubles.

explain.short: Braking distance grows with the square of speed. 2 x 2 = 4, so double speed gives four times the braking distance.
explain.rule: Braking distance grows with the square of speed: 2x speed = 4x, 3x = 9x, 4x = 16x.
explain.trap: 'si quadruplica' (becomes four times) is right: many people wrongly think it only doubles.

sceneParams.caption: Double speed = 4 times the braking distance

q22604.en: The braking distance becomes nine times longer if the speed triples.

explain.short: Braking distance grows with the square of speed. 3 x 3 = 9, so triple speed gives nine times the braking distance.
explain.rule: Braking distance grows with the square of speed: 2x speed = 4x, 3x = 9x, 4x = 16x.
explain.trap: 'nove volte' (nine times), not three times: the speed is squared.

sceneParams.caption: Triple speed = 9 times the braking distance

q22605.en: The braking distance becomes sixteen times longer if the speed quadruples.

explain.short: Braking distance grows with the square of speed. 4 x 4 = 16, so four times the speed gives sixteen times the braking distance.
explain.rule: Braking distance grows with the square of speed: 2x speed = 4x, 3x = 9x, 4x = 16x.
explain.trap: 'sedici volte' (sixteen times), not four times: the speed is squared.

sceneParams.caption: 4 times the speed = 16 times the braking distance

q22606.en: The braking distance does not depend on speed.

explain.short: Speed is the biggest factor in braking distance. The faster you go, the longer it takes to stop.
explain.rule: Braking distance grows with the square of speed: 2x speed = 4x, 3x = 9x, 4x = 16x.
explain.trap: 'indipendente' (independent) is the false word: braking distance depends a lot on speed.

sceneParams.caption: Faster car = much longer braking distance

q22607.en: The braking distance doubles if the speed doubles.

explain.short: When the speed doubles, the braking distance becomes FOUR times longer, not two times. It grows with the square of speed.
explain.rule: Braking distance grows with the square of speed: 2x speed = 4x, 3x = 9x, 4x = 16x.
explain.trap: 'si raddoppia' (doubles) is too little: the right word is 'si quadruplica' (four times).

sceneParams.caption: Double speed = 4 times, not 2 times

q22608.en: The braking distance increases if the grip between tyre and asphalt is low.

explain.short: With low grip the tyres slip more, so the car needs more metres to stop.
explain.rule: Braking distance: longer with low grip, downhill or locked wheels; shorter uphill.
explain.trap: 'aderenza' (grip) 'bassa' (low) means a slippery road: always a longer stop.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip: the car slides longer before stopping
lines: Low grip between tyre and road

q22609.en: The braking distance increases if the road is covered in snow.

explain.short: Snow gives very little grip. The tyres slide and the car needs many more metres to stop.
explain.rule: Braking distance: longer with low grip, downhill or locked wheels; shorter uphill.
explain.trap: 'innevata' (covered in snow) means low grip: braking takes longer.

sceneParams.caption: Snowy road: much longer braking

q22610.en: The braking distance increases if the road is wet.

explain.short: Water between tyre and asphalt lowers grip, so the car needs more metres to stop.
explain.rule: Braking distance: longer with low grip, downhill or locked wheels; shorter uphill.
explain.trap: 'bagnata' (wet) means less grip: braking is longer, never shorter.

sceneParams.caption: Wet road: longer braking

q22611.en: The braking distance increases if the road goes downhill.

explain.short: Downhill, the weight of the car pushes it forward while you brake, so it needs more metres to stop.
explain.rule: Braking distance: longer with low grip, downhill or locked wheels; shorter uphill.
explain.trap: 'in discesa' (downhill) = longer braking; 'in salita' (uphill) = shorter.

sceneParams.caption: Downhill: gravity pushes, braking is longer

q22612.en: The braking distance decreases if the road goes uphill.

explain.short: Uphill, gravity helps to slow the car down, so it stops in fewer metres.
explain.rule: Braking distance: longer with low grip, downhill or locked wheels; shorter uphill.
explain.trap: 'in salita' (uphill) = shorter braking; do not mix it up with 'in discesa' (downhill).

sceneParams.caption: Uphill: gravity helps, braking is shorter

q22613.en: The braking distance decreases if the driver has quick reflexes.

explain.short: Quick reflexes make you START braking sooner, so they shorten the reaction distance. Once you brake, the braking distance stays the same.
explain.rule: Braking distance: longer with low grip, downhill or locked wheels; shorter uphill.
explain.trap: 'riflessi' (reflexes) belong to the reaction distance, not to the 'spazio di frenatura'.

sceneParams.caption: Reflexes change reaction, not braking distance
lines: It depends on speed, road, tyres

q22614.en: The braking distance decreases if the wheels lock.

explain.short: Locked wheels slide on the road and lose grip. The car stops in MORE metres and you cannot steer.
explain.rule: Braking distance: longer with low grip, downhill or locked wheels; shorter uphill.
explain.trap: 'si bloccano' (lock) sounds like strong braking, but a sliding wheel brakes worse.

sceneParams.caption: Locked wheels slide: braking gets longer
lines: Grip is lost, you cannot steer

q22615.en: The braking distance decreases on the downhill side of a hump.

explain.short: After the top of a hump (dosso, a short hill) the road goes down. Downhill the braking distance gets longer, not shorter.
explain.rule: Braking distance: longer with low grip, downhill or locked wheels; shorter uphill.
explain.trap: 'in discesa' (downhill) always means longer braking, also after a 'dosso'.

sceneParams.caption: Downhill side of a hump: braking is longer
lines: Top of the hump, road goes down

q22616.en: The braking distance increases if the road goes uphill.

explain.short: Uphill, gravity helps to slow the car, so the braking distance gets SHORTER, not longer.
explain.rule: Braking distance: longer with low grip, downhill or locked wheels; shorter uphill.
explain.trap: 'aumenta' (increases) is wrong with 'in salita' (uphill): uphill it decreases.

sceneParams.caption: Uphill braking is shorter, not longer

q22617.en: The braking distance decreases if the road goes downhill.

explain.short: Downhill, the car's weight pushes it forward, so the braking distance gets LONGER, not shorter.
explain.rule: Braking distance: longer with low grip, downhill or locked wheels; shorter uphill.
explain.trap: 'diminuisce' (decreases) is wrong with 'in discesa' (downhill): downhill it increases.

sceneParams.caption: Downhill braking is longer, not shorter

q22618.en: The total stopping distance equals the distance travelled during the reaction time plus the distance travelled while braking.

explain.short: First you see the danger and react (reaction distance), then the car brakes to a stop (braking distance). Together they make the stopping distance.
explain.rule: Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance; it depends on speed, tyres and road.
explain.trap: 'più' (plus): the total needs BOTH parts, not only one.

sceneParams.caption: Stopping = reaction distance + braking distance

q22619.en: The total stopping distance depends on speed.

explain.short: The faster you go, the more metres you travel while reacting and while braking. So the stopping distance depends on speed.
explain.rule: Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance; it depends on speed, tyres and road.
explain.trap: 'dipende' (depends) is right: speed changes both parts of the stopping distance.

sceneParams.caption: More speed = longer stopping distance

q22620.en: The total stopping distance depends on tyre wear.

explain.short: Worn tyres grip the road less, so braking takes more metres and the total stopping distance grows.
explain.rule: Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance; it depends on speed, tyres and road.
explain.trap: 'usura' (wear) of the tyres matters: worn tyres = less grip.

sceneParams.caption: Worn tyres: longer stopping distance

q22621.en: The total stopping distance depends on the condition of the asphalt.

explain.short: Wet, icy, dirty or smooth asphalt gives less grip, so the car needs more metres to stop.
explain.rule: Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance; it depends on speed, tyres and road.
explain.trap: 'condizioni dell'asfalto' (road surface condition) changes the grip, so it matters.

sceneParams.caption: Road surface changes the stopping distance

q22622.en: The total stopping distance does not depend on tyre wear.

explain.short: Worn tyres grip less and make braking longer, so the stopping distance DOES depend on them.
explain.rule: Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance; it depends on speed, tyres and road.
explain.trap: 'indipendente' (independent) is the false word: tyre wear matters.

sceneParams.caption: Worn tyres DO make stopping longer

q22623.en: The total stopping distance does not depend on the condition of the asphalt.

explain.short: A wet or icy road surface gives less grip and makes stopping longer, so the asphalt DOES matter.
explain.rule: Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance; it depends on speed, tyres and road.
explain.trap: 'indipendente' (independent) is the false word: the road surface matters.

sceneParams.caption: Road surface DOES change stopping distance

q22624.en: The total stopping distance equals the distance travelled during the reaction time.

explain.short: The reaction distance is only the first part. You must add the braking distance to get the total.
explain.rule: Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance; it depends on speed, tyres and road.
explain.trap: The statement forgets 'più quello percorso durante la frenata' (plus the braking part).

sceneParams.caption: Reaction distance alone is not the total

q22625.en: The total stopping distance equals the distance travelled while braking.

explain.short: The braking distance is only the second part. Before it, you travel some metres while you react. The total is both.
explain.rule: Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance; it depends on speed, tyres and road.
explain.trap: The statement forgets the reaction part: 'spazio totale' needs reaction PLUS braking.

sceneParams.caption: Braking distance alone is not the total

q22626.en: The total stopping distance does not depend on speed.

explain.short: Speed makes both the reaction distance and the braking distance longer. It is the most important factor.
explain.rule: Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance; it depends on speed, tyres and road.
explain.trap: 'non dipende' (does not depend) is false: speed is the main factor.

sceneParams.caption: Speed DOES change stopping distance

q22627.en: The total stopping distance increases if the speed increases.

explain.short: At higher speed you cover more metres while reacting and while braking, so you need more space to stop.
explain.rule: Stopping is longer with more speed, snow, mud or worn tyres.
explain.trap: 'aumenta la velocità' (speed goes up) = longer stop; never the opposite.

sceneParams.caption: More speed = longer stopping distance
lines: More metres to react and brake

q22628.en: The total stopping distance increases if the road is covered in snow.

explain.short: Snow gives very little grip, so braking takes many more metres and the total stop gets longer.
explain.rule: Stopping is longer with more speed, snow, mud or worn tyres.
explain.trap: 'innevata' (snowy) = low grip = longer stop.

sceneParams.caption: Snowy road: longer stopping distance

q22629.en: The total stopping distance increases if the road is covered in mud.

explain.short: Mud is slippery and lowers the grip of the tyres, so the car needs more metres to stop.
explain.rule: Stopping is longer with more speed, snow, mud or worn tyres.
explain.trap: 'fango' (mud) makes the road slippery, like water or snow.

sceneParams.caption: Muddy road: longer stopping distance

q22630.en: The total stopping distance increases if the tyres are worn.

explain.short: Worn tyres grip the road less, especially when wet, so braking takes more metres.
explain.rule: Stopping is longer with more speed, snow, mud or worn tyres.
explain.trap: 'usurati' (worn) tyres = less grip = longer stop.

sceneParams.caption: Worn tyres: longer stopping distance

q22631.en: The total stopping distance increases if the tyres are not worn.

explain.short: Good tyres that are not worn grip well. They do not make the stop longer; worn tyres do.
explain.rule: Stopping is longer with more speed, snow, mud or worn tyres.
explain.trap: Watch the 'non' in 'non sono usurati' (not worn): good tyres help you stop.

sceneParams.caption: Good tyres do not make stopping longer

q22632.en: The total stopping distance increases if the speed decreases.

explain.short: At lower speed you need FEWER metres to react and to brake, so the stopping distance gets shorter.
explain.rule: Stopping is longer with more speed, snow, mud or worn tyres.
explain.trap: 'diminuisce' (decreases): lower speed = shorter stop, not longer.

sceneParams.caption: Lower speed = shorter stopping distance
lines: Fewer metres to react and brake

q22633.en: The total stopping distance increases if the asphalt is rough.

explain.short: Rough asphalt grips the tyres well, so the car stops sooner. Smooth, wet or icy asphalt makes stopping longer.
explain.rule: Stopping is longer with more speed, snow, mud or worn tyres.
explain.trap: 'ruvido' (rough) means good grip, not a slippery road.

sceneParams.caption: Rough asphalt grips well: no longer stop

q22634.en: The driver's concentration affects the safe distance.

explain.short: A driver who is not concentrated reacts later, so the car travels more metres before braking. More distance is needed.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on your speed, attention, load and tyres.
explain.trap: 'concentrazione' (concentration) changes the reaction time, so it matters.

sceneParams.caption: Less focus = later reaction = more distance

q22635.en: The speed you are travelling at affects the safe distance.

explain.short: The faster you go, the more metres you need to react and brake. So the gap must be bigger.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on your speed, attention, load and tyres.
explain.trap: 'velocità' (speed) is the main factor: more speed, bigger gap.

sceneParams.caption: More speed = bigger gap needed

q22636.en: The load carried by the vehicle affects the safe distance.

explain.short: A heavily loaded vehicle is heavier and needs more metres to brake. So you need a bigger gap.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on your speed, attention, load and tyres.
explain.trap: 'carico' (load) means YOUR vehicle's load: more weight, longer braking.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy load = longer braking = bigger gap
lines: It needs more metres to brake

q22637.en: The grip and the condition of the tyres affect the safe distance.

explain.short: Little grip or worn tyres make braking longer. So you must keep a bigger gap.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on your speed, attention, load and tyres.
explain.trap: 'aderenza' (grip) and tyre 'condizioni' (condition) both change the braking distance.

sceneParams.caption: Poor grip or worn tyres = bigger gap

q22639.en: The number of lanes on the road affects the safe distance.

explain.short: The number of lanes does not change how fast you react or brake. The gap depends on speed, road surface, tyres and driver.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on your speed, attention, load and tyres.
explain.trap: 'numero di corsie' (number of lanes) has nothing to do with stopping in time.

sceneParams.caption: Number of lanes does not change the gap
lines: Gap depends on speed, road, tyres

q22640.en: The size of the vehicle in front affects the safe distance.

explain.short: For the quiz, the safe distance depends on YOUR vehicle and YOUR driving: speed, attention, load, tyres, road. The size of the vehicle ahead is not one of these factors.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on your speed, attention, load and tyres.
explain.trap: 'dimensione' (size) of the vehicle ahead is not counted by the quiz; only a risky load ahead is (another question).

sceneParams.caption: Size of the vehicle ahead: not a factor
lines: Small car or big lorry ahead

keywords.en: size of the vehicle in front

q22640.reviewNote: Official FALSE; a large vehicle ahead can block your view, so some learners may find this surprising.

q22641.en: The number of gears in the gearbox affects the safe distance.

explain.short: How many gears the car has does not change reaction or braking. It has nothing to do with the safe distance.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on your speed, attention, load and tyres.
explain.trap: 'numero di marce' (number of gears) is a distractor: it does not affect stopping.

sceneParams.caption: Number of gears does not change the gap

q22642.en: The number of wheels of the vehicle affects the safe distance.

explain.short: The number of wheels is not a factor. The safe distance depends on speed, attention, load, tyre condition and road.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on your speed, attention, load and tyres.
explain.trap: 'numero di ruote' (number of wheels) is a distractor: tyre CONDITION matters, not how many wheels.

sceneParams.caption: Number of wheels does not change the gap
lines: Gap depends on speed and grip

q22643.en: The type of power steering used affects the safe distance to keep from the vehicle in front.

explain.short: Power steering only makes turning the wheel easier. It does not change reaction or braking, so it does not affect the safe distance.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on your speed, attention, load and tyres.
explain.trap: 'servosterzo' (power steering) is about steering, not about stopping.

sceneParams.caption: Power steering does not change the gap

q22644.en: The safe distance does not depend on the type of engine fuel (petrol, diesel, LPG).

explain.short: Petrol, diesel or LPG does not change how fast you react or brake. So the fuel has no effect on the safe distance.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on the driver's health and attention, not on fuel or brakes of others.
explain.trap: Here 'non dipende' (does not depend) is right: the 'alimentazione' (fuel type) is not a factor.

sceneParams.caption: Fuel type has no effect on the gap
lines: Fuel: no effect on the gap

q22645.en: The safe distance depends on the driver's state of health.

explain.short: A driver who is ill or unwell reacts more slowly, so the car travels more metres before braking. The gap must be bigger.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on the driver's health and attention, not on fuel or brakes of others.
explain.trap: 'condizioni di salute' (state of health) changes reaction time, so it matters.

sceneParams.caption: Unwell driver reacts later: bigger gap

q22646.en: The safe distance depends on the driver's attention and concentration while driving.

explain.short: A distracted driver sees the danger later and brakes later. So the gap must be bigger.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on the driver's health and attention, not on fuel or brakes of others.
explain.trap: 'attenzione e concentrazione' (attention and focus) change reaction time.

sceneParams.caption: Distracted driver reacts later: bigger gap

q22647.en: When driving in a queue, it is wise to increase the safe distance, to avoid chain rear-end collisions.

explain.short: In a queue, if the first car brakes, everyone behind must brake too. A bigger gap gives you time and stops a chain of crashes.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on the driver's health and attention, not on fuel or brakes of others.
explain.trap: 'tamponamenti a catena' (chain rear-end crashes) happen when everyone follows too close.

sceneParams.caption: Queue: bigger gap stops chain crashes

q22648.en: The safe distance depends on the power of the vehicle in front.

explain.short: The engine power of the car ahead does not change how fast YOU react and stop. It is not a factor.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on the driver's health and attention, not on fuel or brakes of others.
explain.trap: 'potenza' (engine power) of the vehicle ahead is a distractor.

sceneParams.caption: Power of the car ahead: not a factor
lines: Power: no effect on the gap

q22649.en: The safe distance depends on how well the handbrake works.

explain.short: When driving you stop with the foot brake (service brake). The handbrake is for parking, so it does not set the safe distance.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on the driver's health and attention, not on fuel or brakes of others.
explain.trap: 'freno a mano' (handbrake) is for parking, not for stopping while driving.

sceneParams.caption: Handbrake does not set the gap
lines: You stop with the foot brake

q22650.en: The safe distance depends on whether there are vehicles following behind.

explain.short: The safe distance is the gap to the vehicle IN FRONT. Cars behind you do not change how much space you need to stop.
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on the driver's health and attention, not on fuel or brakes of others.
explain.trap: 'veicoli che seguono' (vehicles behind) are not part of the safe distance in front.

sceneParams.caption: Cars behind do not change the gap ahead
lines: Gap is to the vehicle IN FRONT

q22651.en: The safe distance must be kept only by motor quadricycles.

explain.short: EVERY vehicle must keep a safe distance: cars, motorbikes, lorries and quadricycles (small four-wheeled mini-cars).
explain.rule: Safe distance depends on the driver's health and attention, not on fuel or brakes of others.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is the false word: the rule is for all vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: Every vehicle must keep the safe distance

q22652.en: The safe distance must always be kept, even before starting an overtake.

explain.short: Before overtaking you must not get too close to the car ahead. If it brakes, you must still be able to stop.
explain.rule: Always keep it, enough to stop in time: at least your reaction distance.
explain.trap: 'anche prima di iniziare un sorpasso' (even before overtaking): no exception to 'sempre' (always).

sceneParams.caption: Keep the gap even before you overtake
lines: Car ahead, you want to overtake
Do not close up behind it

q22653.en: The safe distance must be increased if it is hard to predict how the driver in front will behave.

explain.short: If the driver ahead is uncertain or strange, they may brake or turn suddenly. A bigger gap gives you time to react.
explain.rule: Always keep it, enough to stop in time: at least your reaction distance.
explain.trap: 'difficile valutare' (hard to judge) means unpredictable: keep MORE distance.

sceneParams.caption: Unpredictable driver ahead: bigger gap

q22654.en: The safe distance must be such that you can stop the vehicle in time if there is danger.

explain.short: This is the purpose of the safe distance: enough space to stop in time and avoid hitting the vehicle ahead.
explain.rule: Always keep it, enough to stop in time: at least your reaction distance.
explain.trap: 'fermare in tempo' (stop in time) is exactly what the safe distance is for.

sceneParams.caption: Safe gap = enough space to stop in time
lines: You stop in time: no crash

q22655.en: The safe distance must be at least equal to the metres the vehicle travels during the reaction time.

explain.short: The car ahead also needs space to brake, so the minimum gap is what you travel while you react (about 1 second).
explain.rule: Always keep it, enough to stop in time: at least your reaction distance.
explain.trap: 'almeno' (at least): the reaction distance is the minimum, more is better.

sceneParams.caption: Minimum gap = metres travelled in reaction time

q22656.en: The safe distance must always be equal to the vehicle's braking distance.

explain.short: The safe distance is not a fixed copy of the braking distance. It must be at least your reaction distance and grow with speed, road and traffic.
explain.rule: Always keep it, enough to stop in time: at least your reaction distance.
explain.trap: 'sempre uguale' (always equal) is the trap: the gap is not tied to the braking distance alone.

sceneParams.caption: Gap is not 'always equal' to braking distance

q22657.en: The safe distance must be increased when the vehicle in front carries a load that sticks out and is not very stable.

explain.short: A load that sticks out or is unstable may fall onto the road. Stay further back so you can stop or avoid it.
explain.rule: Increase it for risky loads ahead; never reduce it in tunnels, on motorways or behind lorries.
explain.trap: 'sporgente, poco stabile' (sticking out, unstable) is a danger: keep MORE distance.

sceneParams.caption: Unstable load ahead: keep further back
lines: Load could fall on the road

q22658.en: The safe distance must be at least 100 metres in heavy rain.

explain.short: The law does not give a fixed number for rain. The gap must be big enough to stop in time, and in rain it must be bigger than usual.
explain.rule: Increase it for risky loads ahead; never reduce it in tunnels, on motorways or behind lorries.
explain.trap: 'almeno 100 metri' (at least 100 m) is an invented fixed number.

sceneParams.caption: No fixed 100 m: enough to stop in time
lines: Keep a bigger gap than usual

q22659.en: The safe distance can be reduced in tunnels.

explain.short: In a tunnel light and visibility change and a crash is very dangerous. You must never reduce the safe distance there.
explain.rule: Increase it for risky loads ahead; never reduce it in tunnels, on motorways or behind lorries.
explain.trap: 'può essere diminuita' (can be reduced) is false: never reduce it, especially in tunnels.

sceneParams.caption: Never reduce the gap in a tunnel

q22660.en: When driving on the motorway, you can reduce the safe distance, because you do not expect sudden braking from the vehicle in front.

explain.short: On the motorway speeds are high, so stopping distances are long. Sudden braking can always happen: keep a big gap.
explain.rule: Increase it for risky loads ahead; never reduce it in tunnels, on motorways or behind lorries.
explain.trap: 'non ci si aspetta una frenata improvvisa' (no sudden braking expected) is a false excuse.

sceneParams.caption: Motorway: high speed, keep a big gap

q22661.en: If the vehicle in front is a lorry, you must reduce the safe distance, because heavy vehicles have a much longer braking distance than other vehicles.

explain.short: You must never reduce the safe distance behind a lorry. Staying close also hides the road ahead from you.
explain.rule: Increase it for risky loads ahead; never reduce it in tunnels, on motorways or behind lorries.
explain.trap: 'si deve diminuire' (you must reduce) is the false part, and the reason given does not allow it.

sceneParams.caption: Behind a lorry: never reduce the gap
lines: Too close: you see nothing ahead
